chunks: If You punish them, indeed they are Your creatures; if You pardon them, indeed You are mighty and wise.
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'If You punish them, indeed they are Your creatures' in the Quran?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often interpreted as Jesus' humble acknowledgment of God's absolute sovereignty, where 'servants' (ibadaka) emphasizes their dependence on the Divine. It underscores the theological balance between divine justice in punishment and mercy in forgiveness, reflecting the attributes of Al-Aziz (The Mighty) and Al-Hakim (The Wise). This supplication serves as a model for believers to recognize their status as servants while trusting in God's ultimate wisdom and power.
